acceptance: A run reusing an indexless SQLite TPC-H database ends with the helper indexes present (or is rejected with a clear error), proven by a test on the reuse path.
Q21 on the reused SF0.1 DB runs in ~100-250 ms with rows equal to the freshly loaded DB.
Fresh-load behaviour unchanged; sql-execution-gate PASS; affected rerun cell (tpch/sqlite/sf0.1) completes via a fresh load.
description:
Re-scoped after investigation (history://SqliteNullsPlan). The original NULLS LAST theory is disproven: wheel .13 and .17 emit byte-identical Q21 SQL for Netezza and DuckDB sources, and every SQL variant gives the same plan on the same DB. Root cause: the rerun's SF0.1 SQLite DB has zero indexes and no sqlite_stat1. SQLiteAdapter creates nine TPC-H helper indexes only inside load_data; when a run reuses an existing database path, reuse validation accepts the indexless DB and load_data never runs. Adding the 9 helper indexes to a private copy of the same DB (no ANALYZE) restores Q21 from >3 s (interrupted) to 229.7 ms cold / 114.2 ms warm with identical SQL, interpreter and row counts (lineitem 600572, orders 150000). Evidence /tmp/sqlite-plan-index-state.log. A normal fresh run does invoke load_data; no evidence the fresh path fails.
FIX: on reuse, ensure the adapter's helper indexes exist (idempotent CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) or make reuse validation reject a database missing them. Most-correct: a reused DB must be indistinguishable from a freshly loaded one for query plans.
GUARDRAILS: no translation change; no benchmark text change; index creation stays in the adapter's established set; tests must cover the reuse path.
